summary: 1. EX-123 develops a new fault ("Bucket Pin Line Boring," opened 7-Aug) that escalates from a 1-hr breakdown to a full 24-hr stand-down on both Aug 8 and 9 — running simultaneously with EX-253's standing Swing Bearing Failure (day 13+), dragging the excavator fleet to its weakest utilization readings of the cycle (65.0%/67.1%). 2. FCST Week 33-34 forecasts EX-123 returning Aug 14. 2. 3. Production misses widen for three straight days (Aug 7 -3.6%, Aug 8 -22.1%, Aug 9 -19.9%) even as ore beats target on all three (+72.2%, +56.4%, +79.4%) — a waste-side shortfall, not an ore problem. 4. MTD gap widens from -7.8% to -12.1%. 3. 5. The official Maaden Monthly Production Plan lands (666,785 BCM/1,800,318 t) — a third monthly BCM figure alongside the JRAR-internal FCST forecast (760,247 BCM, 14% higher) and the now-superseded provisional survey-workbook target (645,404 BCM, which has been revised to match Maaden's plan exactly). 6. Treated as the authoritative monthly target following the same precedence logic already applied to the weekly Maaden plan deck. 4. 7. A fourth truck ID (DT-346) enters the ongoing DT-108/109-vs-DT-281/282 discrepancy via the FCST Week 33-34 workbook, deepening rather than resolving the conflict the 83rd pass flagged. 5. 8. Blast No. 10 lands (Aug 9, 3,757 BCM) after a six-production-day blast-free run; two blasts earlier in the window (Aug 4, Aug 5) had logged explosive-kg but zero-volume fields, resolved by Blast #9 (Aug 6) populating normally — not a systemic field-population issue. 6. 9. A Class 4 property-damage NCR closes (operator Kaputo Mupeta, Coy #1870) — Maaden's investigation recommends disciplinary action; the operator's leave, held since 27-Jul pending the investigation, can now proceed. Source PDFs are image-only scans; content known only from the covering email. 7. Maaden requests a JRAR assessment of switching ADW pit traffic to left-hand drive, due 13-Aug — a genuine near-term deadline with no response drafted yet. 8. A fifth tire-cost corrective-action thread surfaces: a new standalone Flat Tire Inspection Form, moving toward registration as a JRAR corporate template. 9. A site-wide fire suppression discharge action-plan flow chart is issued to the full ADW Team — image-only source, content known only from the covering email.
